newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president to visit Italy, meet Pope.
newsitem.headline: Polish president to visit Italy, meet Pope.

text.p: Poland's ex-communist President Aleksander Kwasniewski will visit Italy in April 6-8 and is likely to meet Pope John Paul II, PAP news agency said on Tuesday.
PAP quoted presidential spokesman Antoni Styrczula as saying details of the trip were still being worked out but a meeting with the Polish-born Pontiff was planned.

The Pope is due to tour Poland for 11 days starting on May 31 and Kwasniewski has been seeking a meeting before then, as there are some problems between the Catholic church and the ruling ex-communists.
The left-dominated parliament last year passed a law easing Poland's tough restrictions on abortion, and Kwasniewski signed it despite protests from the Pope.

Relations have also been strained by the ex-communists' refusal to ratify a concordat treaty signed by a previous government with the Vatican in 1993, and by differences over the new Polish constitution now being drafted.

Kwasniewski's allies in the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) face a challenge from pro-Catholic, rightist parties in elections due around September, notably a new alliance around the Solidarity union which toppled communist rule in 1989.
The president has been trying to play down religious issues and avoid allowing the Pope's pilgrimage home to become an inspiration for the opposition campaign.

The 42-year-old Kwasniewski has pursued a tough schedule of foreign visits since taking office just over a year ago, largely devoted to promoting Poland's top goals of joining the European Union and NATO and cultivating ties with its neighbours.
